title: Foundation executable specification
description: Objective: author development-only held-out models, fakes, fixtures, and fault schedules for J1, J3, J4, stale clients, and the linear effect boundary. Deliverable: packages/testkit/src/foundation and tests/fault/foundation with fixed fixture hashes and honest expected failures. NOT in scope: production implementation or confirmatory BENCH corpus bytes. Hard dependency: Runtime contract registry. Owned paths: packages/testkit/src/foundation/** and tests/fault/foundation/**. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/testkit typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/testkit test.
definitionOfDone: Fixtures and oracles are deterministic, versioned, hashed, and labeled DEVELOPMENT_ONLY and NOT_CONFIRMATORY.
Schedules cover stale version/lease, cancel-start, crash boundaries, zero-work false green, and honest UNKNOWN.
Missing production behavior fails with named stable outcomes rather than import or placeholder errors.
The focused testkit typecheck and test command exits 0 with expected-red fixtures mechanically distinguished.
taskRails: Follow the pinned design; this task cannot create authority beyond its named contract.
Fail closed with stable codes and immutable deterministic outputs.
Keep production modules focused, target <=250 lines, split before 400.
Use TDD and stage only explicit owned paths; no worktree, broad add, push, or merge.

Landed-surface inventory — verify FRESH with git log + export greps, then re-verify immediately before commit (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` + export grep; the schedule-coverage task was QA-REJECTED for baking FALSE not-landed claims into its manifest — mem:task-task-1de468316...-qa-verdict): LANDED today = @moe/core 4 reducers + TRANSITIONS + identity; @moe/contracts full runtime vocab/registry/envelopes; @moe/store SqliteEventStore FULL commit/decision/outbox/recovery (the J3 transaction begin/write/commit/ack crash boundaries are a BUILT surface — do NOT mark ABSENT); @moe/scheduler graph validate/analyze/preview/frontier exported + authority lease modules landed-but-unexported; @moe/runner workspace; @moe/skills; @moe/mcp stdio. Genuinely ABSENT = core-to-store dispatch composition, ATTEMPT/execution reducer, acceptance/release/terminal management, timers, review assignment, distribution handshake. Stale-lease and store-crash schedules therefore EXECUTE today; the six legacy-incident schedules are mostly ABSENT. Content tripwire: no '@moe/scheduler/' or 'scheduler/src/' literal substrings in any packages/testkit file (boundary walk scans contents; root tests/ exempt).

TDD red — packages/testkit/src/foundation/foundation-spec.test.ts (INSIDE the testkit filter; this is the DoD-4 proof the task's own verification command runs). Assert: (1) expected-outcome vocabulary CLOSED: PASS_EXPECTED | EXPECTED_RED{reason} | PRODUCTION_BEHAVIOR_ABSENT{missingSurface, probeRef} | HONEST_UNKNOWN{missingEvidence}; (2) the foundation expected-outcome manifest (OWN version constant "moe-foundation-expected-outcome/1" — distinct artifact: never reuses moe-schedule-coverage/1, SCHEDULE_* codes, or coverage authority over the schedule-checker's source-derived universe) maps EVERY fixture and schedule to exactly one declared outcome; (3) PARTITION COMPLETENESS: the union of the per-journey partitions the fault tests own equals the full manifest (no hand-picked subset drift); (4) every fixture carries DEVELOPMENT_ONLY + NOT_CONFIRMATORY labels and a pinned sha256 via the LANDED testkit canonicalize/identifyCanonicalEvidence helpers (canonical-json.ts + evidence-digest.ts — never hand-rolled JSON.stringify hashing; identity excludes random IDs/wall timestamps/seeds per the schedule-model precedent); (5) ABSENT entries carry a PROBE REF (see step 4 — no unprobed constants); (6) determinism: two manifest builds byte-identical; zero BENCH-* identifiers anywhere; (7) 'held-out' operationalized: fixture/model files are testkit-resident, labeled advisory, and a source-scan asserts no packages/** production module imports the foundation subdir (fairness-reference precedent — held-out = testkit-only + production-must-not-import + labels; NO hidden-label bytes: the reviewer-calibration corpus is a SEPARATE unowned Phase-1 artifact, flagged to the governor, zero bytes here). Green — foundation-outcomes-fixtures.ts + foundation-model-j1.ts + foundation-model-j3j4.ts (each <=250 hard; per-journey model split pre-planned because one 250-line file cannot hold three journeys — measured density: fairness-model.ts is 162 lines for ONE model). foundation-outcomes-fixtures.ts: the closed outcome vocabulary, the versioned manifest builder, versioned hashed fixture data (canonicalize/identifyCanonicalEvidence reuse, DEVELOPMENT_ONLY + NOT_CONFIRMATORY labels). foundation-model-j1.ts: held-out J1 pure model (design 1095): goal.create -> exact plan/initial-graph approval -> execution -> final acceptance with EXACTLY three human actions; includes the ZERO-WORK FALSE-GREEN oracle self-test hook — the model must REFUSE an attempt trace with no work (empty diff, no artifacts/receipts, green self-claim); anchors CORE-I4 (proof before acceptance), CORE-I14 ('agent text cannot satisfy a gate'), CORE-S1 — a J1 model satisfiable by a no-op trace is itself the false-green defect, and this oracle self-test is executable TODAY (it tests the model, not production). foundation-model-j3j4.ts: J3 crash-recovery model (design 1099: declared crash boundaries, restart record classes adopted/suspect/quarantined/reconciliation, healthy continuation = one safe action creating a traceable binding, never edited history) + J4 rejection/re-plan model (design 1101: findings->evidence links, delta approval with changed hashes + invalidated/carry-forward sets, visible three-round counter, explicit escalation, old artifacts stay readable). Green — foundation-fakes.ts + foundation-fault-schedule.ts + foundation-incident-schedules.ts (incident split pre-planned — six incidents + the DoD-2 catalogue cannot share 250 lines). foundation-fakes.ts: pure injected-port fakes conforming to @moe/contracts envelope shapes (fake dispatch port, fake observation/clock ports — caller-supplied time only) sufficient for the fault tests to drive landed reducers WITHOUT testkit importing them. foundation-fault-schedule.ts: typed schedules for the DoD-2 catalogue — stale version/lease (EXECUTES today against landed contracts registry + authority lease modules via injected ports), cancel-start races, crash boundaries (design-1225 catalogue subset applicable to the LANDED store commit surface — executes today), zero-work false green (the J1 no-op-trace schedule), honest UNKNOWN (missing-evidence schedules asserting HONEST_UNKNOWN, never PASS). foundation-incident-schedules.ts: the six mandatory legacy incident schedules (design 1229): terminal-release-resurrect (53271ca), release-handoff-atomicity (3563791+28a6588), hot-claim-loop (1aa1546), timer-reentrancy (28a6588), silent-review-theft (3d2cb16+b30fb6f), stale-assets handshake — each attempts its production surface through a PRESENCE-DETECTING PROBE: the schedule asserts the named surface is absent from the target package's export set (falsifiable — when the surface lands, the probe goes RED and forces the manifest flip from PRODUCTION_BEHAVIOR_ABSENT to PASS_EXPECTED; the schedule-coverage lockstep pattern; an unprobed constant rots into exactly the false-evidence state QA rejected). comments.content:
GOVERNOR NOTE for whoever claims this next — read before re-running anything.

QA's rejection is correct and the design is not the problem. Do NOT rewrite the specification; QA said so explicitly.

The defect is that this task's DECLARED verification command cannot reach its own owned paths:

  Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/testkit typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/testkit test
  resolves to:  vitest run --root ../.. packages/testkit/src

That glob matches packages/testkit/src only. It does not match tests/fault/foundation/**, which this task also owns. Three files — j1-linear.test.ts, j3-crash.test.ts, j4-replan-stale.test.ts, 43 tests — never executed in the evidence filed as exitCode 0. They pass when run directly. QA confirmed this by mutation, not by reading.

Second, related defect: no tsconfig in the repo includes tests/. packages/testkit/tsconfig.json is include ["src/**/*.ts"] and there is no root tsconfig covering tests/. So tests/fault/foundation/** is neither typechecked nor run by the declared gate.

This is not something a worker can fix by trying harder. Re-running the same command will produce the same false green. You have two legitimate routes:

1. File evidence from a command that actually executes every owned path — e.g. run vitest directly against tests/fault/foundation in addition to the package gate, and state both commands and both tails as evidence. The instruction-contract task set this precedent: it owned tests/instruction-contract/** and gated on `pnpm exec vitest run tests/instruction-contract`, unfiltered, precisely because a package filter cannot see tests/.

2. If you believe the task's declared Verification line must change, say so in #architects before proceeding rather than silently substituting a different command. Changing a task's declared gate is a task-definition decision.

Do not narrow the owned paths to fit the command. The tests are real coverage and dropping them to make the gate honest would be the wrong repair.

General lesson, recorded here because it will recur: any task owning paths under tests/** cannot verify with a `pnpm --filter <pkg>` command. Package filters are scoped to that package's directory. Check that your declared gate's glob actually covers every owned path before filing evidence — a green exit code proves only that whatever ran, passed.
